newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Foreigners seen boosting S.Africa shares next week.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners seen boosting S.Africa shares next week.

text.p: South African shares were seen firm next week on continued foreign buying of local shares and despite concerns that Wall Street's recent slide may not be over, dealers and portfolio managers said on Friday.

The Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) has been the focus of strong offshore interest in the past few weeks. Latest JSE statistics show foreigners have bought shares worth 20.28 billion rand this year compared with 13.93 billion rand in the same period in 1996.
"Foreigners have been buyers of shares on a wide scale and that indicates that the market will go up next week," said Willi Jonker, executive director of portfolio management at Norwich Investments.
Last week alone non-residents were net buyers of 1.24 billion rand's worth of South African shares.
Jonker, however, added that a lot of uncertainty remained in the market, a factor echoed by others and evident in differing views over the JSE's relationship with Wall Street.

"We will continue to depend on Wall Street which is in a corrective consolidation phase. We have seen Wall Street rise to close to its all-time highs but we still cannot believe that its correction is over," one dealer said.
But another was less certain of the close correlation with the U.S. bourse.

"There is a depressing mindset creeping in the market. If Wall Street jumps the local market does not jump. When the U.S. cuts interest rates ours rise. And when theirs rise, our's come down," a dealer said.
South African share gains were, however, seen capped by continued concerns about high local interest rates and the possibility that they might rise again.
Reserve Bank governor Chris Stals said last week that the bank might have to tighten monetary policy further to rein in continued high credit extension and money growth.
Gold shares on the JSE were seen sliding further next week on a bullion price struggling to surface above the $340 level.
"I still think that we will see more downside on gold shares because the reality of a stronger rand and a weaker bullion price has started to sink in," Jonker said.
Traders said there was uncertainty whether bullion had reached bottom.
"It is tempting to think that the gold price is at bottom. If you want to buy golds, rather go for companies that at least pays higher dividends," one dealer advised.
There are no major South African economic indicators due for release next week, but eyes will be focused on a number of large companies which will announce earnings.
Companies in the South African Breweries stable, including Edgars Stores Ltd and Plate Glass & Shatterprufe Industries Ltd, are due to report. Analysts have forecast weaker earnings for both firms.

The banking sector also kicks off its reporting season. First National Bank Holdings Ltd starts on Wednesday and is expected to post flat half year earnings, trailing robust growth at fellow banks Nedcor Ltd and Amalgamated Banks of South Africa Ltd, which report later in May.
